title: West Chester moves to repeal its $1.2 million stream protection fee
summary: Borough Council holds a public hearing Wednesday, Sept. 16 on repealing the Stream Protection Fee ordinance, which raised about $1.2 million a year before collection stopped April 30 following a state Supreme Court ruling that the charge functioned as a tax. How stormwater work gets paid for instead — property taxes, parking rates or reduced spending — will be settled in the 2027 budget.

title: Chester County measles count climbs to 65 cases
summary: Nine new cases in the past week put the county third in Pennsylvania behind Lancaster and Mifflin in what state officials call the worst measles outbreak here in more than three decades. County health officials are asking residents to check their vaccination status, noting a blood test can confirm immunity when records are missing.

title: Netflix's 'Tires' co-creator still calls West Chester home
summary: Steve Gerben, who co-created and stars in the Netflix comedy Tires alongside Shane Gillis, films the show in an addition to his father's former tire shop on East Gay Street and golfs weekly on West Chester courses. The series was renewed for a fourth season after its Aug. 13 season-three premiere drew 2.4 million views in its first weekend.

title: West Chester starts enforcing its 35-gallon trash can limit after Sept. 30
summary: The borough's updated garbage ordinance caps curbside trash cans at 35 gallons, and Public Works says larger cans will stop being collected once a grace period ends Sept. 30, with fines possible after that. The borough says it has no approved alternative for households that need bigger containers.

title: Neighbors raise $88K to restore Everhart Park's 1908 gazebo
summary: The Friends of Everhart Park are funding a restoration of the park's rustic cedar-and-fieldstone gazebo over Black Horse Run entirely through private donations, with about $55,000 of the $88,000 goal raised. Work starts with hand-shaped red cedar guardrails and refurbished benches, followed by a new rot-resistant shingle roof on the National Register-listed structure.

title: Rustin grad's nicotine step-down device is now in 70 UK pharmacies
summary: Zachary Starr founded Quix Labs at 16 after watching classmates at West Chester Rustin High School struggle with nicotine; now 23 and a 2024 West Chester University graduate, he sells its Quixotic refillable inhaler in roughly 70 pharmacies across England. The nine-person company kept its headquarters in West Goshen and is aiming to submit for FDA review by 2028.

title: 14 West Chester students named National Merit semifinalists
summary: Henderson High School led the area with seven semifinalists, followed by four at Pennsylvania Leadership Charter School, two at Rustin and one at East. The students now move on to the finalist round, with scholarship winners chosen next spring.

title: Spring freeze leaves Highland Orchards with a sliver of its apple crop
summary: After an April warm spell was followed by a hard freeze, Highland Orchards expects roughly 5 percent of a normal apple harvest, so pick-your-own will run shorter hours with far fewer varieties this fall. Hayrides, the corn maze and crops the freeze spared are still going ahead.

title: Urban Cutz barbershop opens in a hidden courtyard off High Street
summary: Longtime local barber Gerome Ruff and his wife Monica opened their own shop, reached by a brick walkway beside Barnaby's. It's styled as a speakeasy-feel, old-school barbershop and is the couple's first business.

title: West Chester Co-op opens its community-owned grocery downtown
summary: After more than ten years of organizing, the member-owned market opened Aug. 21 and runs 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily. It stocks produce, bulk goods and grab-and-go food, much of it from area farms and makers, and has more than 830 members.
